channel.title: Car Recall Tracker — new vehicle recalls
channel.description: NHTSA vehicle safety recalls explained in plain English.

item.title: Rivian R1S and R1T backup camera display issue
item.description: In some Rivian R1S and R1T vehicles, a notification can pop up on screen and block part of the rearview camera image when the vehicle is in reverse. This can make it harder for the driver to see what is behind the vehicle while backing up.

item.title: Volkswagen Atlas And Tiguan Steering Bolt May Break
item.description: This recall covers certain Volkswagen Tiguan and Atlas SUVs, along with related Audi Q3 vehicles. A bolt that attaches the steering rack to the subframe can corrode, or rust, and break over time. If that bolt breaks, the steering rack housing itself can break as well, affecting the steering system on these vehicles. The bolt involved is located on the right side of the steering rack.

item.title: Jeep Wagoneer Roof Rack Crossbars May Come Loose
item.description: Chrysler is recalling certain Jeep Wagoneer, Wagoneer L, Grand Wagoneer, and Grand Wagoneer L vehicles because the pivot bolts holding the roof rack crossbars may not have been tightened correctly. This could let the crossbars come loose and detach from the roof while the vehicle is being driven, rather than staying securely attached as intended.

item.title: Volkswagen Tiguan Software Glitch Can Stall Engine
item.description: A software error can cause the body control module in the vehicle to reset itself. This can make the ignition switch off, which then stalls the engine. The same software error can also cause a loss of certain vehicle controls, warning lights, and exterior lighting. It can also cause the rearview camera system to stop working properly, affecting several parts of the vehicle at once.

item.title: Toyota RAV4, Tundra Hybrid Weight Label Error
item.description: The label on your vehicle that shows the load carrying capacity modification may display an inaccurate added weight value. This means the number telling you how much extra weight your vehicle can carry may not be correct. Dealers will replace the load carrying capacity modification label with a corrected one, free of charge, once new labels are ready to be mailed to owners.

item.title: Jeep Grand Cherokee Rear Coil Spring May Detach
item.description: On these Jeep Grand Cherokee models, the rear coil springs may have been installed incorrectly. Because of this, a spring can come loose and separate from the vehicle while you are driving. This recall replaces two earlier recalls for the same problem, and vehicles already repaired under those earlier recalls will still need this new fix.

item.title: Jeep tire pressure warning system may miss low tires
item.description: Chrysler is recalling certain Jeep Grand Cherokee, Grand Cherokee L, Grand Cherokee 4xe, Wagoneer, Wagoneer L, Grand Wagoneer and Cherokee vehicles. A software error means the tire pressure monitoring system may not detect a tire that is low, or may not turn on the tire pressure warning light the way it should. Because of this, the vehicles do not meet the federal standard for tire pressure monitoring systems. Dealers will update the software free of charge.

item.title: Chrysler Pacifica Sensor Crack May Disable Stability Control
item.description: In these vehicles, a small part inside the brake pedal position sensor, called a capacitor, may develop a crack. This crack can cause the vehicle's electronic stability control to stop working while the vehicle is being driven. Dealers will inspect the brake pedal position sensor on affected vehicles and replace the sensor if a crack is found, and this repair will be done free of charge to the owner.

item.title: Ford Mustang Wiring Can Cause Power Loss
item.description: The engine compartment wiring harness has ground connections that can crack or break over time. If that happens, the vehicle can lose the power that keeps it moving forward. The same wiring problem can also cause other systems to stop working, including the windshield washers, the headlights, the air conditioning, or the engine cooling fan, depending on which connection is affected.

item.title: Outlander Rearview Camera May Not Display
item.description: Mitsubishi is recalling certain Outlander and Outlander PHEV vehicles because of a software problem in the vehicle's infotainment system. Due to improper programming, the system may fail to show the rearview camera image on the screen when the vehicle is put into reverse. This means the driver may not be able to see the picture from the rearview camera while backing up, which does not meet federal rear visibility requirements.

item.title: Kia EV9 air bag may not detect a child
item.description: Kia America is recalling certain 2025-2026 EV9 vehicles. Because of improper routing, the system meant to detect a child or child seat in the front passenger seat and turn off the air bag may not work as intended, so the air bag may not deactivate when it should.

item.title: Ford F-650 Liftgate Deck Pins May Break
item.description: On this truck, the deck pins that hold the liftgate platform in place may break. If a pin breaks, the liftgate platform can fall unexpectedly, which increases the risk of injury to anyone nearby.

item.title: Buick and Chevrolet Rearview Camera May Show Blank Image
item.description: General Motors is recalling certain Buick Envista, Buick Encore GX, Chevrolet Trailblazer, and Chevrolet Trax vehicles because the rearview camera screen may display a distorted or blank image instead of showing what's behind the vehicle clearly.

item.title: Dodge Durango Rear Spoiler Detachment Risk
item.description: On some Dodge Durango vehicles, the rear spoiler may not line up correctly with the roof. Because of this, the spoiler can get damaged when the liftgate is opened or closed. A damaged spoiler could eventually come loose from the vehicle. A spoiler that falls off onto the road creates a hazard for other drivers, which raises the risk of a crash.

item.title: Chevrolet Silverado, GMC Sierra 2500 tire pressure label wrong
item.description: General Motors is recalling certain Chevrolet Silverado 2500 and GMC Sierra 2500 trucks built with the enhanced towing option and the 20-inch accessory tire and wheel package. The label that lists tire pressures may show the wrong pressure for the rear tires. Going by it can leave those tires underinflated, and it can also keep the truck's tire pressure monitoring system from showing a low tire pressure warning. Dealers will inspect, update software, add a corrected label overlay, and set the tires to the right pressure as needed, free of charge.

item.title: Nissan Altima Passenger Air Bag May Not Deploy
item.description: Certain 2025 Nissan Altima vehicles may have had the front passenger air bag and the front passenger knee air bag installed with incorrect mounting fasteners. Because of this, these air bags may not deploy as intended if the vehicle is in a crash. This affects the front passenger seating position in affected vehicles, where both the main air bag and the knee air bag could be affected.

item.title: BMW M550i Driveshaft Connection May Fail
item.description: On certain BMW vehicles including the M550i xDrive, the connection between the driveshaft and the rear differential can become damaged. This can cause a loss of power to the rear wheels while driving, or it can lead to the vehicle rolling away on its own if the parking brake isn't set. A sudden loss of power increases the risk of a crash, and an unexpected rollaway increases the risk of a crash or injury.

item.title: BMW X3 Steering Spindle May Be Loose
item.description: On certain BMW X3 vehicles, the steering spindle—the part that connects the steering wheel to the steering column—may not have been properly attached. This is a problem with the physical connection inside the steering system, between the steering wheel and the column beneath it. If this connection is not secure, the way the vehicle steers could be affected.

item.title: Dodge Hornet, Alfa Romeo Tonale Seat Belts May Not Retract
item.description: On these Dodge Hornet and Alfa Romeo Tonale vehicles, the rear seat belts next to the windows can become twisted. When that happens, the belt may not pull back in the way it should. A belt that does not retract properly may not hold an occupant in place the way it is meant to. Dealers will replace the retractors, the parts that wind the belt in and out, at no cost to the owner.

item.title: Toyota Tacoma Shock Absorber Reservoir Can Detach
item.description: On some Toyota Tacoma vehicles, a metal flange on the front and rear shock absorbers may corrode. If it corrodes enough to fail, the external oil reservoir attached to the shock absorber can detach from the vehicle.

item.title: Camry Hybrid Cluster Failure Disables Warning Lights
item.description: Some 2025-2026 Camry Hybrid vehicles may have an instrument cluster display that fails to work when the vehicle is started. If that happens, the hazard lights, turn signals, seat belt warning system, and smart key reminder can all be deactivated at the same time.

item.title: Rivian R1S and R1T Front Turn Signals May Fail
item.description: On certain Rivian R1S and R1T vehicles, one or both of the front turn signals may fail to light up and flash. Because the front turn signals may not work, these vehicles do not meet the federal safety standard for lights and reflectors. Rivian will have the front turn signals inspected and replaced if needed, at no cost. This recall expands an earlier Rivian recall, number 25V387.

item.title: Volvo VNL and VNR trucks may lose roof marker lights
item.description: Volvo Trucks North America is recalling certain 2026-2027 VNL (4) and VNR (4) trucks. The center marker lights on the roof of the cab may fail to light up. Because of that, these trucks do not meet the federal rule for lamps, reflectors and related equipment. Dealers will replace the center roof marker light free of charge. Owner notification letters are expected to be mailed October 5, 2026, and the affected VINs will be searchable on NHTSA.gov starting August 13, 2026.

item.title: Tesla Model 3 and Model Y Headlights Too Bright
item.description: On certain Tesla Model 3 and Model Y vehicles, the low beam headlights may shine brighter than they are allowed to be. Headlights that are too bright can reduce how well oncoming drivers are able to see the road, other vehicles, and their surroundings. This reduced visibility for drivers coming the other way raises the chance of a crash happening.

item.title: Honda CMX300, CMX500 Handlebar Lock Screw May Loosen
item.description: Certain Honda CMX300 and CMX500 motorcycles, along with the Honda SCL500, have a screw that locks the handlebar in place. This lock screw can loosen over time and detach completely. If the screw comes loose, it may lodge between the motorcycle's frame and the steering stem, getting in the way of how the handlebars turn. This recall expands an earlier Honda recall that covered the same handlebar lock screw issue.

item.title: Ram 1500 Rear Seat Belt Anchor Problem
item.description: Certain Ram 1500 trucks may have a problem with the seat belt buckles in the second row. The anchors that attach the center and left-side seat belt buckles to the vehicle may not have been installed correctly. Because of this, these seat belts may not properly hold occupants in place during a crash, which increases the risk of injury. These vehicles do not meet a federal safety standard for seat belt anchorages.

item.title: Cadillac Escalade IQ, Hummer EV Battery Fire Risk
item.description: Certain Cadillac Escalade IQ, Escalade IQL and GMC Hummer EV Pickup vehicles may have a problem with the high voltage battery. An internal component inside the battery may not be properly secured in place. If this component becomes loose, it can move around inside the battery and cause damage to it. Damage to the high voltage battery in this way increases the risk of a fire.

item.title: Mercedes-Benz Door Lock Defect May Cause Rollaway
item.description: Certain Mercedes-Benz vehicles have a micro-switch in the driver's door lock that can corrode. When this happens, the switch may fail to detect that the door is open, which can prevent the electronic parking brake's Auto-Park feature from engaging on its own. Without the parking brake engaging automatically, the vehicle may roll away on its own.

item.title: BMW S 1000 RR Ignition Lock May Fail
item.description: On some BMW S 1000 RR motorcycles, vibration can cause a part inside the ignition lock to fail. This can knock out the instrument display, rear lighting, and other systems like ABS, or cause the engine to stall while you're riding. BMW is still developing a repair. In the meantime, the company is mailing letters to let owners know about this safety risk.

item.title: VW Atlas rearview camera image may not display
item.description: These vehicles may experience a low-voltage electrical event that affects the display screen's functions. When this happens, the rearview camera image may fail to show up as it should. This affects certain Volkswagen Atlas and Atlas Cross Sport vehicles equipped with this display and camera system. Volkswagen is recalling the affected vehicles to update the rearview camera software so the image displays correctly.

item.title: Ford Explorer, Lincoln Aviator Seats May Recline
item.description: Some Ford Explorer and Lincoln Aviator vehicles have a driver's seat that may recline on its own when no one is sitting in it, such as when the vehicle is remotely unlocked or remotely started. If the seat back moves unexpectedly, it could trap a person sitting in the second row.

item.title: Ford Bronco Engine Wiring Can Short Circuit
item.description: The wiring harness in the engine compartment of your Ford Bronco or Bronco Raptor may become damaged. If the wiring is damaged, it can short-circuit, meaning electricity arcs where it shouldn't. This can create heat or a spark in the engine compartment.

item.title: Nissan Armada and Infiniti QX80 Incorrect Weight Label
item.description: On certain Nissan Armada and Infiniti QX56/QX80 vehicles equipped with 22-inch wheels, the axle weight rating shown on the vehicle's certification label is incorrect. Because the number is wrong, an owner could load the vehicle beyond what it can safely carry. Nissan will correct the problem by installing new certification labels on the vehicle and mailing replacement labels directly to owners.

item.title: Ford, Lincoln Second-Row Seats May Shift Unexpectedly
item.description: Ford is recalling certain Explorer and Lincoln Aviator vehicles because the switch for the easy-entry second-row outer seats may bind or stick. This can cause the seat to unlatch, tip, or slide unexpectedly. A seat that moves unexpectedly may not properly restrain a passenger in a crash. This is a phased recall — the repair will become available at different times depending on the model and model year. Dealers will inspect and replace the switch bezel as necessary, at no cost.

item.title: Ford Explorer Roof Rail Covers May Detach
item.description: On certain Ford Explorer vehicles, the covers on the roof rails may come loose and detach from the vehicle.

item.title: Hyundai Kona Rear Center Seat Belt Buckle May Fail
item.description: Some Hyundai Kona and Kona Electric vehicles have a seat belt buckle in the rear center seat that may not properly hold a passenger in place if the vehicle is in a crash. This means that seat position may not provide the protection a seat belt is supposed to give during a collision.

item.title: Volvo Truck Steering Arm May Loosen, Crash Risk
item.description: Volvo Trucks is recalling certain trucks because the steering knuckles may have been built with the steering arms not tightened enough. A loose steering arm can affect the vehicle's steering, since the connection between the steering arm and the steering knuckle isn't as secure as it should be. This loss of a secure connection can make it harder for the driver to steer the truck as intended.

item.title: Subaru Ascent and Forester have wrong weight rating label
item.description: Subaru is recalling certain Crosstrek Hybrid, Forester, Forester Hybrid and Ascent vehicles. The certification label on these vehicles shows an incorrect Gross Axle Weight Rating, the maximum weight an axle is rated to carry. Because of this, the vehicles do not meet a federal safety standard covering tire and rim selection. Subaru will mail owners a new label free of charge, and owners who prefer can have a dealer install the new label instead, also free.

item.title: Model 3 Vehicles Missing Required Safety Features
item.description: Certain Tesla vehicles were originally built for a foreign market and do not have knee air bags. They may also be missing certain interior safety features and may not have been tested for bumper impact resistance. Because of this, these vehicles do not meet federal safety standards for occupant crash protection, interior impact protection, and bumper standards.

item.title: Hyundai Ioniq 5 Battery Cells Risk Fire
item.description: Certain Hyundai Ioniq 5 vehicles have high voltage battery cells that may contain misaligned electrodes inside them. This kind of misalignment inside the battery can lead to a fire, and this can happen whether the vehicle is parked or being driven at the time.
